sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Foundational Principle 1**: The term 'Ecosystem' was coined by **A.G. Tansley (1935)**, emphasizing the integration of biotic and abiotic components.
• **Foundational Principle 2**: Ecosystems are **open systems** characterized by constant input/output of energy and matter.
• **Foundational Principle 3**: Ecosystems exhibit **homeostasis** (self-regulation) and **resilience** (capacity to recover from disturbance).
• **Key Metric / Factor**: **Trophic structure** and **Energy flow** (unidirectional) are the primary determinants of ecosystem stability.

items.definition: A zone of transition between two distinct communities (e.g., Mangroves between terrestrial and marine ecosystems). High biodiversity due to the 'Edge Effect'.
The functional role and position of a species within its environment, including its resource use and interactions. No two species can occupy the same niche indefinitely (Gause's Principle).

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Ecosystem Services**: Provisioning, Regulating, Cultural, and Supporting services (Millennium Ecosystem Assessment).
• **Nature-based Solutions (NbS)**: IUCN-led initiatives to address societal challenges through ecosystem management.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Key Challenges**: Habitat fragmentation, invasive species, and climate-induced shifts.
• **Solutions**: Ecosystem-based Adaptation (EbA) and landscape-level conservation.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym / Phrase**: 'T-A-N-S-L-E-Y' (Tansley coined Ecosystem).
• **Decoded Meaning**: T-Total, A-Abiotic, N-Nature, S-System, L-Living, E-Energy, Y-Yield.

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: Confusing 'Ecosystem' with 'Biome'. A Biome is a large-scale climatic region (e.g., Tundra), while an Ecosystem is a functional unit that can be as small as a pond.
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Ecological Integrity' when discussing developmental projects in ecologically sensitive zones.

keyTakeaways: Ecosystems are defined by functional interactions, not just physical boundaries.
Energy flows unidirectionally, while nutrients cycle within the ecosystem.
The 'Edge Effect' in ecotones is a high-yield concept for Prelims.
